title: The Rise of Temujin
description: 1186-1206. Follow Temujin's unification of the Mongol tribes on the steppe: rescue his wife Borte from the Merkits, forge and then break the alliance with Jamukha, defeat the Naiman confederation, and be proclaimed Genghis Khan at the kurultai. The player begins with a small warband and must grow through raids, alliances, and decisive battles.

anachronisms_found: CAMEL_RIDER x3 in the enemy (Merkit/Jamukha/Naiman) roster — camel riders are a Middle Eastern/Saracen unit type; steppe tribes of the Onon-Kerulen fought as horse archers and light lancers, and the engine already supplies those

KING x2 used to represent the Merkit chieftain and Tayang Khan — the King is a crowned Western European monarch model, an avoidable mismatch when Mongol-appropriate cavalry or hero units could stand in for a steppe chieftain

GUARD_TOWER x2 plus PALISADE_WALL x10 and a GATE for a nomadic Merkit/Naiman camp — masonry guard towers are inappropriate for mobile steppe encampments; palisade alone would have been defensible enough

GENGHIS_KHAN hero unit deployed from 1186, i.e. twenty years before Temujin received that title at the 1206 kurultai (mitigated by it being the same historical person and the only Mongol hero the engine offers)

issues_found: Both the Merkit chieftain and Tayang Khan of the Naiman are represented by the generic KING unit — a crowned European monarch model, culturally wrong for steppe tribal leaders. The engine ships mounted steppe-era heroes (e.g. Kushluk, historically Tayang Khan's own son; Subotai) that would have been far closer, so this is avoidable.

Jamukha, named repeatedly in the narration as blood-brother, ally, and then betrayer, is never placed or created as a unit — his 'betrayal' is only a spawn of anonymous CAVALRY_ARCHER/LIGHT_CAVALRY. The scenario's central relationship has no on-map embodiment.

Toghrul/Wang Khan and the Kereit confederation, indispensable to Temujin's rise (and to the actual Borte rescue and the later war that preceded the Naiman campaign), are entirely absent — only two players are active.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins, and tech could render as Teutonic, Britons, or anything else; Mongols was available and should have been assigned to at least Player 1.
CAMEL_RIDER x3 in the Naiman roster is wrong: the Naiman were a Turkic-Mongol steppe horse-archer confederation, and the AoE2 camel rider is a Middle Eastern unit with no place on the Altai steppe.

The Naiman camp is defined by PALISADE_WALL x10, a GATE and two GUARD_TOWERs — a sedentary fortified enclosure, whereas Tayang Khan's host was a mobile nomadic camp (the yurts placed alongside are correct; the masonry towers are not).

The chronology of the Borte rescue is inverted: historically Temujin recovered Borte from the Merkits *with* Jamukha's and Toghrul's armies; here the Jamukha alliance is triggered only after the Merkit chieftain is already dead.
Only 106 objects on a 120x120 map means the 'unification of the tribes' is fought against a single enemy camp; the plurality of tribes (Tatars, Kereits, Taichiud) the brief promises is unrepresented.

Both active players are assigned civilization RANDOM, so the Merkit/Naiman and Mongol camps may render with any architecture set and receive any tech tree - avoidable, since Mongols (and e.g. Huns/Tatars) are available and would fix both look and unit access.
Player 2 fields CAMEL_RIDER x3; camel cavalry belongs to Saracen/desert rosters, not Merkit or Naiman steppe tribes, and light cavalry or cavalry archers were available substitutes.

Both enemy leaders (the Merkit chieftain and Tayang Khan) are the generic KING unit - a European crowned monarch model - rather than a renamed mounted unit, which would read far better as a steppe chieftain.

Jamukha, named repeatedly in the narration as blood-brother and then betrayer, exists only as CREATE_OBJECT spawns; no unit stands in for him, so the scenario's central personal rivalry has no on-map embodiment.

Toghrul/Wang Khan of the Kereits is entirely absent, yet he was Temujin's principal patron in the Borte rescue and the decisive 1203 war immediately preceding the Naiman campaign - the unification is therefore compressed to Merkit, Jamukha, Naiman only.
The alliance with Jamukha is triggered after the Merkit chieftain's death, whereas in the sources Jamukha (with Toghrul) fought alongside Temujin in the raid that recovered Borte.
A single ARCHERY_RANGE and STABLE are the only military production buildings - with random civs their appearance and available units are unconstrained for a nomadic camp of yurts.

The victory trigger fires on destruction of a KING owned by player 2, but player 2 owns two KINGs, so the intended target (Tayang Khan rather than the Merkit chieftain) is not pinned by the condition itself.
